transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-10-29
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Avery Chen (Redwood AE), Maya Patel (Redwood SE), Liam Torres (Cedar Grove Head of Search), Priya Kapoor (Cedar Grove ML Eng), Ethan Wu (Cedar Grove PM)
Shared artifacts: relevance-playbook deck (https://redwood.example/decks/relevance-playbook), Console quickstart (link shared in chat), pilot spreadsheet (internal link)

Summary (auto): Quick hosted API demo focused on embeddings + reranking flows, walked through Redwood Console routing and Optimize recommendations. Customer asked about latency/cost tradeoffs and data residency; team agreed to pilot with 3K doc subset.

Topics: Hosted embeddings endpoint, reranker endpoint, scoring strategies, caching/prefix cache, batching, console observability, SOC2/audit logs, pilot scoping

Transcript:
[00:00:01] Avery Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. My name's Avery, I'm the AE on this. We've got about 45 minutes, we'll do a quick walk through of the hosted API for embeddings and the reranker, then show the Console suggestions via Optimize. Maya from engineering will demo.
[00:00:12] Liam Torres: Thanks, Avery. Quick note, we're juggling a launch window for late Q1 so timeline's tight, want to understand perf and cost.
[00:00:18] Maya Patel: Great, hi all. I'll try to keep this practical, show the API calls, then the console, and a few notes on best practices for production.
[00:00:27] Priya Kapoor: Sounds good. Our stack is Node backend + Elastic for indexing today, and we sent over a sample of about 3k docs.
[00:00:33] Ethan Wu: Also DM: stakeholders are engineering + product and legal wants to know data flow for compliance.
[00:00:45] Maya Patel: Cool. So first slide, embeddings endpoint. We support fixed-dim and dynamic dims depending on model; call pattern is simple POST /v1/embeddings with the model param. Example payloads in the quickstart.
[00:00:58] Speaker 1: (inaudible) — sorry, quick q, do you host vectors or do customers manage storage?
[00:01:06] Avery Chen: Good question. For hosted we return vectors and customers can store them in their vector DB of choice — we intentionally don't force a particular vector store. Many customers use Pinecone or self-managed Faiss or Elastic with vector plugin. We also provide embeddings-as-a-service with optional persistence for enterprise plans.
[00:01:25] Liam Torres: So for our pilot we'd store in Elastic. Any recommendations on dimensionality vs retrieval latency?
[00:01:33] Maya Patel: Yes — in practice 768-1536 dims is a sweet spot for semantic search; smaller dims reduce storage and slightly speed up kNN, but you lose nuance. We can recommend model variants in Optimize based on your query mix.
[00:01:45] Priya Kapoor: What about batching? We have thousands of documents to embed initially.
[00:01:50] Maya Patel: There's automatic batching in the hosted API — you can send up to N items in a single call (see docs). For initial ingestion we suggest 512–2048 document batches depending on payload size. The Console has an ingestion throughput indicator that will show estimated tokens per second and expected cost.
[00:02:10] [00:02:11] Maya Patel: I'll switch to the reranker demo now. Reranker is a two-step flow: retrieve top-k with embeddings, then call the rerank endpoint with the query + candidate list. The reranker returns calibrated scores and explanations if you enable structured output.
[00:02:26] [00:02:30] Priya Kapoor: Is the reranker model separate? How do you handle KV cache?
[00:02:34] Maya Patel: Reranker is a separate endpoint — it's optimized for pointwise and pairwise scoring. For hosted low-latency use we use smaller encoder-decoder variants that keep memory usage minimal; KV cache isn't really in play for rerank since it's not autoregressive generation. For chat generation workloads we manage KV caches and continuous batching.
[00:02:52] Liam Torres: Latency numbers, ballpark?
[00:02:55] Maya Patel: For rerank alone, p50 on a standard hosted tier is ~45–90ms for a single item depending on model. If you're running retrieve+rerank for top-10, end-to-end p95 can be 120–350ms depending on network and vector DB time. We have dashboards in Console to break down per-stage latency.
[00:03:14] Ethan Wu: The p95 range is wide — what's the biggest lever to bring this down?
[00:03:18] Maya Patel: Biggest levers: lowering top-k, using smaller reranker model, colocating your vector DB in same region, and prefix/KV caching of frequent queries. Also batching for ingestion but that's separate.
[00:03:29] [00:03:35] Avery Chen: Also worth noting Redwood Optimize will run workload analysis and recommend model + quantization profiles that can cut cost 30–60% with small quality regression checks.
[00:03:45] Priya Kapoor: Can you explain quantization a bit? We haven't done that in prod.
[00:03:49] Maya Patel: Sure — we support INT8 and 4-bit quantized variants for many open models. Optimize will suggest quantization when your evals show minimal quality delta on your prompt set. We also provide rollbacks and canary deployments so you can test quantized model in a small portion of traffic.
[00:04:06] [00:04:12] Liam Torres: On security — we need SOC2 reports, SSO and ability to keep logs for 1 year, and keys integrated with our KMS.
[00:04:20] Avery Chen: We're SOC 2 Type II; we have SSO via SAML/Okta, role-based access controls in Console, and we support customer-managed keys via KMS for Private deployments. For hosted we offer encrypted-at-rest and configurable retention for logs and transcripts; we can also provide audit logs exports. I'll attach SOC2 and security pack after.
[00:04:40] Priya Kapoor: Is data used for model training? That's a strict no for us.
[00:04:44] Avery Chen: For hosted, customer data is not used for training by default — we have a privacy opt-out and enterprise contracts that explicitly forbid training use. We can include this in the contractual terms for the pilot.
[00:04:54] [00:05:00] Maya Patel: Back to practicals — I'll demo a live sample. (screen share) Here is a sample query, we call embeddings, store vectors in the customer's Elastic, then run a top-50 retrieval, then rerank.
[00:05:12] [00:05:18] Maya Patel: (typing noises) Sorry if the screenshare blips — network is a hair laggy today. Okay, sent the POST to /v1/embeddings — response shows vector length 1024. Now a retrieve operation against Elastic returns 50 candidates. Now call /v1/rerank with query + candidate bodies.
[00:05:37] [00:05:45] Speaker 2: The score outputs had decimals, what's the interpretation?
[00:05:47] Maya Patel: Scores are normalized probabilities with calibration applied; higher is better. The endpoint can return top-N with highlights and structured reasoning if you enable that flag. That helps product teams show snippets with rationale.
[00:06:00] Liam Torres: Do you support rerank-by-feature — like boosting recency or exact-match signals?
[00:06:05] Maya Patel: Yes — you can include auxiliary features per candidate (e.g., recency, click-through rate, domain score) and the reranker will incorporate them. There's an example JSON in the quickstart.
[00:06:15] [00:06:20] Priya Kapoor: About cost — can you give a simple model: embeddings cost + rerank cost per call?
[00:06:25] Avery Chen: Roughly, hosted embeddings are billed per-embedding unit (token or doc) and rerank is per-invocation plus per-item for candidate scoring on some pricing tiers. We'll share a tailored price sheet for your projected qps. The pilot pricing can be capped for the first month.
[00:06:41] Ethan Wu: Do you have examples of production customers who did the retrieve-rerank hosted flow?
[00:06:46] Avery Chen: Yes — a couple of newsroom and e-commerce customers. We can share anonymized latency/cost matrices; I'll attach a one-pager.
[00:06:55] [00:07:05] Maya Patel: Now, Console — this is where you can configure model routes, rollouts, and see per-token cost. (screen) On the left is model catalog, we recommend a baseline model and a quantized candidate. You can define a route that sends 80% traffic to baseline and 20% to quantized for canary.
[00:07:22] Maya Patel: There's also an Optimize tab that analyzes request logs and suggests batching, cache windows, and model swaps. For example it suggested enabling a 30s prefix cache for one customer which reduced tokens by 18% on their mix.
[00:07:35] Liam Torres: How does caching interact with freshness? We have time-sensitive content.
[00:07:40] Maya Patel: You can set TTL at the route level and exclude queries matching freshness patterns. Caching is best for FAQ-ish queries or product detail lookups. For breaking news you can bypass cache or have short TTLs.
[00:07:51] [00:08:00] Priya Kapoor: Technical deep dive: if we wanted private deployment later, how much of the Console and Optimize features would be available?
[00:08:06] Avery Chen: Private (VPC) includes the same Console features via a private control plane; some telemetry can be shipped to your account only. We have an on-prem package where we can run the inference runtime behind your firewall and the control plane can be in your VPC. We'll sync with Solutions for detailed architecture.
[00:08:22] Ethan Wu: Any specific pre-req infra? We use Kubernetes and have on-prem object store.
[00:08:27] Maya Patel: Kubernetes is supported; object storage for model artifacts is required. We have an install guide; SEs will help size GPUs for expected qps. For Dedicated vs Private we'll size GPU pools and discuss autoscaling policies.
[00:08:40] [00:09:00] Maya Patel: One more thing on quality — we recommend evaluating with a held-out query set. Optimize's eval runner will run model A/B comparisons and show MRR and nDCG metrics. You can hook that into the Console to trigger regressions alerts.
[00:09:14] Liam Torres: On the pilot, what success metrics should we use?
[00:09:17] Avery Chen: Common pilot metrics: improvement in MRR/nDCG vs current baseline, median end-to-end latency under X ms, and cost per 1k queries. Also subjective content relevance from product team.
[00:09:29] Priya Kapoor: We'd like to keep p95 under 300ms if possible.
[00:09:33] Maya Patel: Totally reasonable for top-10 + rerank with colocated vector store and smaller reranker model. We'll include configuration options to meet that SLO.
[00:09:44] [00:10:05] (brief side conversation about dataset formatting, timestamps missing in sample)
[00:10:12] Liam Torres: On instrumentation — can we export traces to our Datadog?
[00:10:16] Avery Chen: Yes, Console supports exporting traces and logs to common APMs like Datadog; we also provide webhook and S3 delivery for raw logs.
[00:10:25] Ethan Wu: Any concerns about vendor lock-in?
[00:10:28] Avery Chen: We try to minimize lock-in: same API surface across hosted/dedicated/private, model version pinning, and you can always self-host models later. We also provide a migration guide and export tools for artifacts.
[00:10:40] [00:11:00] Maya Patel: Demo wrap-up: I'll run one more demo showing Optimize suggestions. (screen) Optimize scanned 24k sample queries and suggests: reduce embedding dim for infrequent queries, enable 20s prefix cache for low-cardinality queries, and swap to quantized reranker for 10% traffic. Each suggestion shows projected cost delta and expected quality delta.
[00:11:25] Priya Kapoor: Those projected deltas are useful. We will need to see the actual evaluation on our queries.
[00:11:30] Maya Patel: Absolutely — that's why pilot includes an evaluation phase. We'll run A/B on your provided sample set.
[00:11:38] [00:11:45] Avery Chen: Quick commercial note: for pilot we typically do a 30-day scoped pilot with capped usage. If pilot looks good we can move to reserved Dedicated or continue hosted with volume discounts.
[00:11:57] Liam Torres: Legal will need standard data terms, we need KMS integration detail.
[00:12:03] Avery Chen: I'll send the security pack and contract template.
[00:12:09] Ethan Wu: Anything else on the roadmap that might affect us?
[00:12:13] Maya Patel: We're rolling out more advanced rerank explainability and a feature store integration next quarter. Also improving console trace granularity for pipeline stages.
[00:12:24] [00:12:40] (silence as people skim shared docs)
[00:12:52] Priya Kapoor: One last technical question — can the reranker consume raw HTML content or do we need to sanitize?
[00:12:58] Maya Patel: You should strip scripts and heavy markup; we accept sanitized HTML snippets or text. There's a small tokenizer hit if you include lots of markup, it's best to send cleaned text.
[00:13:10] Liam Torres: Ok, that covers my major points. Next steps recap?
[00:13:15] Avery Chen: Recap: Avery to send pricing + SOC2/security pack + architecture diagram; Maya to share console recording and quickstart snippets; Liam to send final 3k sample subset and 5 canonical queries for evaluation. Pilot kickoff tentatively next week if legal is quick.
[00:13:33] Ethan Wu: We'll aim to get the sample over by Friday.
[00:13:36] Priya Kapoor: I'll validate formats and send a short spec doc.
[00:13:40] [00:13:45] (end screen share)
[00:13:50] Avery Chen: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email.
[00:13:55] Liam Torres: Thanks, appreciate it.
[00:14:00] (meeting ends early — discussion moved to email)

Notes on transcript quality: Some speaker labels are generic and occasional transcription errors (model names and product terms spelled inconsistently). Live demo timestamps approximate.
